In [[mathematics]], the '''conductor–discriminant formula''' or '''Führerdiskriminantenproduktformel''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Helmut Hasse|last=Hasse|year1=1926|year2=1930}} for [[abelian extension]]s and by  {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Emil Artin|last=Artin|year=1931}} for [[Galois extension]]s,  is a formula calculating the relative [[discriminant of an algebraic number field|discriminant]] of a finite Galois extension <math>L/K</math> of [[local field|local]] or [[global field]]s from the [[Artin conductor]]s of the [[character theory|irreducible characters]] <math>\mathrm{Irr}(G)</math> of the [[Galois group]] <math>G = G(L/K)</math>.

== Statement ==
Let <math>L/K</math> be a finite Galois extension of global fields with Galois group <math>G</math>. Then the [[discriminant of an algebraic number field|discriminant]] equals

:: <math>\mathfrak{d}_{L/K} = \prod_{\chi \in \mathrm{Irr}(G)}\mathfrak{f}(\chi)^{\chi(1)},</math>

where <math>\mathfrak{f}(\chi)</math> equals the global [[Artin conductor]] of <math>\chi</math>.{{sfn|Neukirch|1999|loc=VII.11.9}}

== Example ==
Let <math>L = \mathbf{Q}(\zeta_{p^n})/\mathbf{Q}</math> be a [[cyclotomic field|cyclotomic extension]] of the rationals. The Galois group <math>G</math> equals <math>(\mathbf{Z}/p^n)^\times</math>. Because <math>(p)</math> is the only finite prime ramified, the global Artin conductor <math>\mathfrak{f}(\chi)</math> equals the local one <math>\mathfrak{f}_{(p)}(\chi)</math>. Because <math>G</math> is abelian, every non-trivial irreducible character <math>\chi</math> is of degree <math>1 = \chi(1)</math>. Then, the local Artin conductor of <math>\chi</math> equals the conductor of the <math>\mathfrak{p}</math>-adic completion of <math>L^\chi = L^{\mathrm{ker}(\chi)}/\mathbf{Q}</math>, i.e. <math>(p)^{n_p}</math>, where <math>n_p</math> is the smallest natural number such that <math>U_{\mathbf{Q}_p}^{(n_p)} \subseteq N_{L^\chi_\mathfrak{p}/\mathbf{Q}_p}(U_{L^\chi_\mathfrak{p}})</math>. If <math>p > 2</math>, the Galois group <math>G(L_\mathfrak{p}/\mathbf{Q}_p) = G(L/\mathbf{Q}) = (\mathbf{Z}/p^n)^\times</math> is cyclic of order <math>\varphi(p^n)</math>, and by [[local class field theory]] and using that <math>U_{\mathbf{Q}_p}/U^{(k)}_{\mathbf{Q}_p} = (\mathbf{Z}/p^k)^\times</math> one sees easily that if <math>\chi</math> factors through a primitive character of <math>(\mathbf{Z}/p^i)^\times</math>, then <math>\mathfrak{f}_{(p)}(\chi) = p^i</math> whence as there are <math>\varphi(p^i) - \varphi(p^{i-1}) </math> primitive characters of <math>(\mathbf{Z}/p^i)^\times</math> we obtain from the formula <math>\mathfrak{d}_{L/\mathbf{Q}} = (p^{\varphi(p^n)(n - 1/(p-1))})</math>, the exponent is

::<math> \sum_{i = 0}^{n} (\varphi(p^i) - \varphi(p^{i-1}))i = n\varphi(p^n) - 1 - (p-1)\sum_{i=0}^{n-2}p^i = n\varphi(p^n) - p^{n-1}.</math>
